title: Choose something you enjoy
prompt: What would you like? Point, tap, sign, or say it.
caregiver_tip: Offer a real choice you can honor. Wait without counting down.

title: Ask for help
prompt: You can ask for help in your own way.
caregiver_tip: Model help during a real activity. Never withhold needed help to get a response.

title: Choose a break
prompt: Would you like a break or to finish? Both are okay.
caregiver_tip: Honor the choice immediately. A break is not something to earn.

title: Your answer matters
prompt: Would you like a book? Yes, no, and not sure are all okay.
caregiver_tip: Ask about something available. Accept the answer without correcting it.

title: Tell me what you need
prompt: You can tell someone what you need.
caregiver_tip: Keep water accessible. Do not make communication a condition for basic needs.

title: How do you feel?
prompt: Choose a feeling, or choose not sure.
caregiver_tip: Do not assign a feeling from facial expression. The child can decline.

title: Make your space comfortable
prompt: What would help you feel comfortable?
caregiver_tip: Reduce noise or give space when requested. No eye contact is required.

title: More or all done?
prompt: Would you like more, or are you all done?
caregiver_tip: Follow the child's lead. Stop when they indicate all done.

title: Share a book
prompt: Choose a book or a different activity.
caregiver_tip: Comment on a picture the child notices. Avoid turning every page into a quiz.

title: Invite someone to play
prompt: Would you like company or some space?
caregiver_tip: Parallel play counts as connection. Do not demand turn-taking.

title: Ask for more time
prompt: You can ask someone to wait.
caregiver_tip: Give processing time and honor a request to wait.

title: Choose what comes next
prompt: Which activity would you like next?
caregiver_tip: Show two real options. Either choice, including no, is valid.

title: Explore the word more
prompt: Listen to 'more', tap more, or try the word if you want.
caregiver_tip: Model naturally once. No repetition quota or pronunciation score.

title: Explore the word book
prompt: Look at a book. You can listen, point, tap, or say 'book'.
caregiver_tip: Accept every communication mode. Follow existing clinician guidance for speech goals.

title: Explore the word play
prompt: Choose play, listen to the word, or say it your way.
caregiver_tip: Do not correct an accent or speech difference. This is optional word play.

title: Try a short message
prompt: Try 'more play' with speech, signs, or the message strip.
caregiver_tip: Model a short phrase without requiring imitation.

title: Check in with yourself
prompt: How are you feeling? You can choose not sure.
caregiver_tip: Listen without arguing. Offer support, not a label.

title: You can say stop
prompt: Stop is always a message you can use.
caregiver_tip: Honor stop immediately. Never practice by creating distress.
